researchers.name: Petar Hadžić
researchers.title: Assistant Professor
researchers.bio: Petar Hadžić completed his Bachelor's and Master's degrees in Computer Science at the Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2010 and 2012 respectively, followed by a PhD in 2017 on delta-encoding and dictionary compression for columnar sensor databases. He joined the Department of Mathematics and Informatics as a Teaching Assistant in 2013 and was promoted to Assistant Professor in 2018. His research group focuses on efficient storage and query processing of high-frequency time-series data generated by industrial and environmental sensors, targeting commodity x86 hardware without specialised accelerators. He teaches undergraduate courses in Database Systems and Data Structures, and a graduate course in Advanced Query Processing. The group operates a small cluster of off-the-shelf servers instrumented with custom data acquisition boards and uses open-source columnar database engines as experimental platforms.
open_to: contract research on time-series storage and query optimisation
joint projects with companies generating high-frequency sensor data
industrial PhD supervision for candidates employed at NTP companies
student internships (BSc and MSc level) involving real sensor datasets
consulting on columnar database schema design and codec selection
equipment access (NVMe cluster) for benchmarking under a formal agreement
researchers.industry_experience: During 2019–2020 Hadžić provided paid technical consulting to a regional utilities company on the migration of their SCADA historian database to a columnar storage backend, covering codec configuration and query tuning. He has no other formal industry employment.
researchers.notes: Hadžić has expressed a preference for collaborations where the company can share raw sensor data for publication-quality experiments, even under anonymisation agreements. He is currently supervising two PhD students and has capacity for one additional industrial PhD candidate from late 2025 onward.

researchers.name: Branislav Lekić
researchers.title: Research Associate
researchers.bio: Branislav Lekić completed his BSc and MSc in Geodesy and Geoinformatics at the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, graduating in 2014 and 2016 respectively. He received his PhD from the same institution in 2022, with a dissertation on parcel-level crop yield estimation using dense Sentinel-2 time series fused with meteorological reanalysis data. He joined the Remote Sensing and GIS Group at the BioSense Institute as a Research Associate in 2022, where the group focuses on satellite-based agricultural monitoring, land-cover mapping, and precision farming decision support. He contributed to teaching exercises in the GIS and Remote Sensing courses at the Faculty of Technical Sciences. His experimental work relies on the group's high-performance computing cluster, Google Earth Engine, and ground-truth yield data collected via collaboration with local agricultural cooperatives.
open_to: joint projects
contract research
consulting
researchers.industry_experience: During the CROPSENSE project Lekić worked directly with staff from three agricultural cooperatives to collect combine-harvester yield records and validate satellite-based estimates, gaining practical experience in translating research outputs into formats usable by field agronomists.
researchers.notes: Left the University of Novi Sad in March 2026; now a postdoctoral researcher at a university in Austria. Profile not updated. Enquiries regarding ongoing collaboration or access to the CROPSENSE dataset should be directed to the Remote Sensing and GIS Group at BioSense Institute.

researchers.name: Snežana Marković
researchers.title: Professor Emeritus
researchers.bio: Snežana Marković completed her medical degree at the University of Novi Sad Faculty of Medicine in 1978 and her doctoral dissertation in diagnostic radiology at the University of Belgrade in 1989. She spent her entire academic career at the Faculty of Medicine in Novi Sad, reaching the rank of Full Professor in 2001 and retiring as Professor Emeritus in 2017. Her research focused on measuring and reducing occupational radiation doses in interventional fluoroscopy suites, including the development of department-level dose optimisation protocols for cardiologists, radiologists, and nursing staff. She supervised the Radiation Protection Laboratory at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, where the group used ionisation chambers, thermoluminescent dosimeters, and real-time electronic personal dosimeters. She taught radiation protection to medical students and residents for over three decades.
open_to: consulting
researchers.industry_experience: Professor Marković provided expert consultation to two regional hospital procurement committees during fluoroscopy equipment tender processes in 2008 and 2014, advising on dose management capabilities and shielding specifications.
researchers.notes: Retired since 2017; available for consulting engagements on a limited basis, particularly in the areas of dose optimisation protocol development, radiation protection audits for interventional suites, and review of occupational monitoring programmes. Not available for project coordination or laboratory work. Prefers written communication in the first instance.

researchers.name: Emilija Tešić
researchers.title: Full Professor
researchers.bio: Emilija Tešić received her BSc and MSc degrees in Mathematics and Computer Science from the University of Novi Sad in 2001 and 2004, respectively, and completed her PhD at the same institution in 2009 with a dissertation on formal verification methods for inference systems. She joined the Department of Mathematics and Informatics as an assistant professor in 2010 and was promoted to full professor in 2020. Her research group focuses on explainability frameworks for machine learning models, automated detection of factual inconsistencies in large language model outputs, and grounding mechanisms that link generated text to verifiable source documents in retrieval-augmented generation pipelines. She teaches courses in logic programming, knowledge representation, and applied machine learning. The group regularly uses the Faculty's GPU cluster and maintains shared annotation infrastructure for benchmarking hallucination detection datasets.

researchers.industry_experience: Tešić collaborated with a regional legal information provider during the VERIFAI-RS project, advising on requirements and evaluating a prototype verification module against real workflows. She has provided informal consulting to two software companies in Novi Sad on explainability reporting requirements under EU AI regulations.
researchers.notes: Tešić is on a reduced teaching load in the 2025–2026 academic year following her term as vice-dean, which gives her more time for research collaborations than in the previous two years. She has a preference for collaborations that involve concrete evaluation datasets and measurable technical deliverables rather than purely exploratory engagements.

researchers.name: Nina Mamužić
researchers.title: Senior Research Associate
researchers.bio: Nina Mamužić completed her undergraduate and master's studies in Food Technology at the Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad, graduating in 2005 and 2007 respectively. She obtained her PhD in 2013 from the same institution, with a dissertation on the microencapsulation of lipid-rich plant extracts in protein-polysaccharide carriers. She joined the Department of Food Preservation Engineering as a Research Associate in 2014 and was promoted to Senior Research Associate in 2020. Her group focuses on spray-drying and freeze-drying encapsulation of oxidation-sensitive lipids, wall material formulation, and in vitro digestion modelling. She teaches elective courses in food packaging and functional food technology at the master's level. The laboratory is equipped with a Büchi B-290 spray dryer, a TA Instruments DSC, HPLC with fluorescence detection, a Malvern Zetasizer, and a Rancimat unit for accelerated oxidation testing.

This engagement ran from 2017 to 2018 and informed the selection of raw material specifications used in subsequent academic studies.
researchers.notes: Vesna Mitrović has expressed interest in partnerships with companies at NTP Novi Sad that produce plant-based food supplements, functional dairy, or bakery ingredients, particularly those seeking to add omega-3 claims to their products. She is not currently on sabbatical and is available for collaborative discussions. Her laboratory capacity for spray drying is shared with two other research groups, so large-scale contract work would require scheduling coordination.

Njena istraživačka grupa bavi se merjenjem zrelosti upravljanja znanjem u javnim institucijama, sa posebnim fokusom na tranzicione ekonomije centralne i jugoistočne Evrope. Predaje predmete Menadžment znanja, Organizaciono učenje i Upravljanje promenama. U radu koristi softver za kvalitativnu analizu (ATLAS.ti) i alate za statističku obradu podataka (SPSS, R), kao i institucionalne baze podataka opština i javnih preduzeća u Vojvodini.

researchers.name: Ljiljana Bačić
researchers.title: Associate Professor
researchers.bio: Ljiljana Bačić completed her law degree at the Faculty of Law, University of Novi Sad (2003), her master's degree at the same institution (2007), and her doctoral thesis on testamentary freedom under the influence of post-socialist legal reform at the Faculty of Law, University of Ljubljana (2013). She joined the Department of Civil Law in Novi Sad as an assistant in 2008 and was promoted to Associate Professor in 2019. Her research focuses on succession law reform across Central and South-Eastern European legal systems, examining how post-socialist states have renegotiated the balance between testamentary freedom and forced heirship. She collaborates regularly with legal scholars in Hungary, Croatia, Slovenia, and Austria. She teaches courses on inheritance law and family property law, and her group uses comparative legal databases, archival legislative materials, and empirical survey data collected from notarial practice.

researchers.notes: Bačić is a member of the Faculty of Law Civil Code drafting working group, which meets monthly and limits her availability for new commitments during the 2025–2026 academic year. She has expressed interest in collaborating with legal technology or digital estate management companies but has not previously worked in that sector and would expect an initial scoping discussion before committing to a project. She reads Croatian, Slovenian, Hungarian (with difficulty), German, and English in addition to Serbian.

researchers.name: Valentina Stojanović
researchers.title: Associate Professor
researchers.department: Department of Computing and Control Engineering
researchers.bio: Valentina Stojanović received her B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Computer Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2004 and 2007 respectively, and her Ph.D. in 2012 from the same institution with a dissertation on mutation-based adequacy criteria for embedded control software. She was appointed Assistant Professor in 2013 and Associate Professor in 2018. Her group focuses on formal specification languages for firmware behaviour, automated generation of test suites from state-machine and contract-based models, and regression testing strategies for resource-constrained embedded systems. She teaches courses on software testing, formal methods, and embedded systems at both undergraduate and graduate levels. The group uses a lab equipped with JTAG debuggers, hardware-in-the-loop rigs, and several microcontroller development platforms for validation experiments.

researchers.industry_experience: Stojanović conducted a two-year action research collaboration with a regional industrial electronics firm producing programmable logic controllers, contributing to the introduction of formal specification practices in their firmware development workflow. She has provided short-term consulting to two additional companies in the automotive electronics sector on test adequacy assessment.
researchers.notes: Stojanović has a preference for collaborations where research access to real firmware codebases or development histories is possible; anonymised datasets are acceptable. The lab has hardware-in-the-loop rigs available for collaborative experiments. She is not seeking pure consulting arrangements but is open to industry contracts that include a research output component.

researchers.name: Ана Рајић

Дипломирала је 2001. и докторирала 2009. године на истом факултету, са тезом о протоколима за безбедну дистрибуцију фирмвера у индустријским мрежама са ограниченим пропусним опсегом. Њена истраживачка група бави се аутентификацијом и интегритетом фирмвера у телеметријским системима са прекидном бежичном везом, укључујући LPWAN технологије и индустријске SCADA окружења. Предаје курсеве из безбедности уграђених система и протокола бежичних мрежа. Лабораторија располаже опремом за емулацију деградираних канала, LoRaWAN и Zigbee развојним платформама, као и алатима за формалну верификацију криптографских протокола.

researchers.name: Đurđica Kuzmanović

researchers.bio: Đurđica Kuzmanović completed her undergraduate and master's studies in Serbian language and linguistics at the Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad, and defended her doctoral dissertation on cross-lingual morphological tagging in 2013 at the same institution. She was appointed Assistant Professor in 2014 and promoted to Associate Professor in 2019. Her research group focuses on building annotated corpora and computational resources for morphologically rich languages, particularly Serbian, Croatian, Hungarian, and Finnish, with an emphasis on transfer learning across typologically distant language families. She teaches courses in corpus linguistics, computational morphology, and natural language processing at both undergraduate and postgraduate level. The group works primarily within the Laboratory for Language Technologies at the Faculty of Philosophy, making use of shared HPC resources through the Academic Network of Serbia.

researchers.name: Petar Krstić
researchers.title: Full Professor
researchers.bio: Petar Krstić received his BSc and MSc degrees in Business Informatics from the Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad, in 2000 and 2003 respectively, and completed his PhD at the same faculty in 2009 with a dissertation on ontology-driven data integration in public administration. He was appointed Full Professor in 2018. His research group focuses on semantic web technologies, controlled vocabularies, and interoperability frameworks applied to public e-procurement across Western Balkan and EU accession contexts. He teaches Database Systems, Knowledge Representation, and e-Government courses at both undergraduate and postgraduate levels. The group uses the Protégé ontology editor, Apache Jena, and OpenLink Virtuoso triple stores hosted on faculty servers, and maintains a curated corpus of machine-readable procurement notices drawn from national public procurement portals.

researchers.title: viši naučni saradnik
researchers.department: Department of Fruit Growing, Viticulture, Horticulture and Landscape Architecture
researchers.bio: Attila Kovács diplomirao je na Poljoprivrednom fakultetu Univerziteta u Novom Sadu 2003. godine, a doktorat iz oblasti vinogradarstva i zemljišne mikrobiologije odbranio je 2010. godine na istom fakultetu. Od 2011. radi kao istraživač na Departmanu za voćarstvo, vinogradarstvo, hortikulturu i pejzažnu arhitekturu, a zvanje višeg istraživača saradnika stekao je 2017. godine. Njegova istraživačka grupa proučava zajednice arbuskularne mikorize i ektomikorize u organskim i konvencionalnim vinogradima na padinama Fruške gore, sa posebnim naglaskom na sezonal dinamiku, uticaj agrotehnike i simbiotske interakcije sa sortama Vitis vinifera. U nastavi pokriva kurseve iz vinogradarstva i zaštite bilja. Laboratorijsku analizu obavlja primenom metoda amplikonskog sekvenciranja (Illumina MiSeq), qPCR i mikromorfoloških tehnika.
open_to: Zajednički projekti sa kompanijama koje se bave mikoriznim inokulantima ili biostimulatorsima
Ugovorna istraživanja: testiranje efikasnosti AMF preparata u lokalnim uslovima
Konzalting u oblasti organske vinogradarske sertifikacije i zdravlja zemljišta
Pristup opremi: Illumina MiSeq amplikon sekvenciranje, qPCR, mikroskopija
Studentske prakse za studente agronomije, ekologije ili biotehnologije
researchers.industry_experience: Kovács je u periodu 2019–2020. godine sarađivao sa jednim vojvođanskim rasadničarskim preduzećem na evaluaciji komercijalnih mikoriznih preparata za sadnice vinove loze, pri čemu su rezultati te saradnje objavljeni u naučnoj literaturi.
researchers.notes: Kovács preferira istraživačka partnerstva koja podrazumevaju terenski rad na lokacijama unutar 60 km od Novog Sada. Zainteresovan je za saradnju sa kompanijama koje razvijaju dijagnostičke alate za monitoring zdravlja zemljišta, naročito ako postoji mogućnost kalibracije metoda na postojećim skupovima podataka iz Fruške gore.

researchers.name: Nikola Orlović
researchers.title: Full Professor
researchers.bio: Nikola Orlović received his undergraduate and master's degrees from the Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad, and completed his PhD at the Faculty of Law, University of Ljubljana in 2009, with a dissertation on the cross-border enforceability of sukuk contracts in civil-law systems. He joined the Department of Finance and Banking in Subotica as an assistant professor in 2010 and was promoted to full professor in 2021. His research group examines the structural mechanics of Islamic finance instruments—sukuk, murabaha, ijara, and musharaka—alongside their treatment under EU capital-adequacy directives, Serbian banking law, and Central European contract law. He teaches courses on financial regulation, comparative banking law, and alternative finance. The group works with legal databases (HeinOnline, Westlaw), AAOIFI standards documentation, and regulatory filings from the European Banking Authority.
open_to: joint projects with fintech or banking companies exploring shariah-compliant product design
contract research on regulatory compliance for alternative finance products
consulting on Islamic finance regulatory strategy for financial institutions entering Serbian or regional markets
co-supervision of doctoral students working on financial law or alternative finance
participation in industry working groups or advisory panels on financial regulation
researchers.industry_experience: Orlović served as an external legal-regulatory consultant to a regional commercial bank in Sarajevo during 2018–2019, advising on the feasibility of introducing murabaha home-purchase financing under Bosnian banking law. He has provided written expert opinions to the National Bank of Serbia on three occasions relating to the classification of atypical financial instruments.
researchers.notes: Orlović has no laboratory infrastructure but makes extensive use of legal and financial databases available through the University of Novi Sad library. He is comfortable engaging with technology companies if the use case touches on regulatory technology (RegTech) for Islamic finance compliance monitoring or automated shariah-screening tools. He reads Arabic at a functional level (legal texts) but does not teach in Arabic.

researchers.name: Mirjana Jeremić
researchers.title: Associate Professor
researchers.department: Department of Civil Engineering and Geodesy
fields: Remote Sensing and Non-Destructive Subsurface Investigation
researchers.bio: Mirjana Jeremić received her Diploma Engineer degree in Geodesy from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2004, and her PhD in Civil Engineering and Geodesy from the same institution in 2012. She joined the Department of Civil Engineering and Geodesy as a Teaching Assistant in 2005 and was promoted to Associate Professor in 2019. Her research group focuses on locating and mapping buried utilities using ground-penetrating radar, GNSS and total-station surveying, and the integration of survey results into GIS-based utility cadastres for water, gas, and electricity distribution networks. She teaches courses in Engineering Geodesy and Geoinformation Systems. The group uses a GSSI SIR-4000 GPR system, Leica TS16 total stations, and ArcGIS and QGIS environments for cadastre compilation.
open_to: contract research – GPR surveys and utility cadastre construction for infrastructure projects
consulting – subsurface utility engineering methodology and regulatory compliance
joint projects – smart city underground asset management, cross-border spatial data harmonisation
industrial PhD supervision – candidates with engineering or geomatics background
student internships – geodesy and GIS students, minimum 3-month placements
equipment access – GSSI SIR-4000 GPR system available for joint surveys under formal agreement
researchers.industry_experience: Jeremić has provided technical consulting on GPR survey design and utility cadastre specification to two regional distribution operators and one municipal public utility company since 2016. She served as expert reviewer for the geodetic component of a 14 km underground cable project in Srem between 2020 and 2021.
researchers.notes: Prefers industry partners who can provide genuine access to operational network records, as anonymised or aggregated data limits research depth. Currently supervising two doctoral candidates; capacity for a third industrial PhD candidate exists from mid-2025 onward.

researchers.name: Đorđe Nikolić
researchers.title: Assistant Professor
researchers.bio: Đorđe Nikolić received his B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Traffic Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2008 and 2011 respectively, and his Ph.D. from the same institution in 2016. His doctoral research addressed metaheuristic approaches to multi-depot vehicle routing under time-window constraints for infrastructure maintenance fleets. He joined the Department of Traffic Engineering as a Teaching Assistant in 2012 and was appointed Assistant Professor in 2018. His group works on combinatorial optimisation problems in logistics and maintenance operations, with particular focus on geographically dispersed road and utility network assets. Teaching responsibilities include courses in transport logistics, operations research, and traffic flow theory. The group regularly uses CPLEX, OR-Tools, and a Python-based simulation environment running on departmental cluster hardware.
open_to: joint projects with logistics or infrastructure companies
contract research on route optimisation and fleet scheduling
industrial PhD supervision
student internships in algorithm development or data analysis
consulting on maintenance logistics planning
access to OR-Tools and CPLEX modelling environment for short-term collaborations
researchers.industry_experience: Nikolić provided consulting support to a regional utility company in Novi Sad during 2020–2021 on restructuring their maintenance crew dispatch procedures, resulting in revised scheduling protocols and a reduction in overtime hours. He has also participated in two short-term technical assistance engagements with provincial road authorities as part of the MAINTAIN-X project.
researchers.notes: Nikolić is currently supervising two doctoral students and has limited capacity for new large projects before mid-2026. He is particularly interested in collaborations that provide access to real operational data from maintenance or logistics companies, as synthetic benchmarks are a recognised limitation of the group's current work. He is open to co-supervision arrangements with industry partners at NTP Novi Sad.

researchers.name: Урош Симић
researchers.title: доцент
researchers.bio: Урош Симић је дипломирао на Технолошком факултету Универзитета у Новом Саду 2009. године, где је одбранио и докторску дисертацију 2016. године на тему механистичког моделовања растварања хидрофилних матрикс таблета. Након краткотрајног постдокторског боравка на Универзитету у Љубљани (2016–2018), враћа се на матични факултет, где је изабран у звање асистента, а затим доцента 2021. године. Истраживачки рад усмерен је на дизајн контролисаног ослобађања лекова из хидрофилних матрикса и мултичестичних система, уз примену механистичких модела растварања. Група располаже опремом за таблетирање, флуидизовано уређај за пелетирање, апаратима за испитивање растварања USP II и III, те HPLC системом. Симић изводи наставу из Фармацеутског инжењерства и Технологије лекова.
open_to: индустријски PhD надзор
уговорна истраживања
консултантске услуге из области испитивања растварања и механистичког моделовања
приступ опреми (USP апарати за растварање, HPLC, флуидизовани уређај за пелетирање)
студентске стручне праксе
researchers.industry_experience: Симић је у периоду 2019–2020. обављао консултантске услуге за домаћег произвођача генеричких лекова у вези са оптимизацијом процеса производње таблета с продуженим ослобађањем и успостављањем спецификација растварања.
researchers.notes: Симић је заинтересован за сарадњу са компанијама које се баве развојем генеричких или иновативних оралних лекова с контролисаним ослобађањем, посебно у области примене механистичких модела растварања за смањење обима in vitro и in vivo испитивања. Предност даје пројектима у трајању 1–3 године са јасно дефинисаним испорукама. Тренутно нема слободних места за постдоктора, али може да прихвати до два магистарска/докторска студента на индустријским темама.

researchers.name: Róbert Pásztor
researchers.title: Full Professor
researchers.department: Department of Administrative and Public Law
researchers.bio: Róbert Pásztor completed his undergraduate and doctoral studies at the University of Novi Sad Faculty of Law, receiving his doctorate in 2007 with a dissertation on administrative discretion in Serbian public law. He held a postdoctoral fellowship at the University of Vienna Faculty of Law (2008–2010) before returning to Novi Sad, where he was appointed Full Professor in 2019. His research focuses on the legal obligations imposed on operators of automated and algorithmic decision-making systems, particularly under the EU Artificial Intelligence Act and related European administrative law frameworks. His group examines transparency requirements, conformity documentation, and fundamental rights impact assessments for high-risk AI systems in public administration. He teaches administrative law and EU digital regulation at undergraduate and postgraduate level, and regularly uses legal databases (EUR-Lex, HUDOC) and document analysis software in his work.
open_to: contract research on regulatory compliance analysis for AI systems
consulting on EU AI Act compliance documentation and procedures
joint projects on AI governance with companies developing high-risk AI systems for public sector clients
student internships for law students interested in technology regulation
participation as external legal expert in product conformity assessment processes
researchers.industry_experience: Pásztor has provided legal opinions to two Serbian public bodies on the lawfulness of deploying vendor-supplied risk-scoring systems for social benefit eligibility. He has no prior employment in the private sector.
researchers.notes: Pásztor reads and works in Serbian, Hungarian, English, and German, which facilitates engagement with Central European and German-speaking partners. He is particularly interested in working with companies at NTP Novi Sad that supply AI systems to public administrations and need independent legal analysis of their compliance documentation before market entry. He has no laboratory infrastructure and no patents; his contribution to collaborative projects is entirely analytical and legal.

researchers.name: Ljubomir Orlović
researchers.title: Assistant Professor
researchers.bio: Ljubomir Orlović completed his undergraduate and master's studies in Chemical Engineering at the Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad, graduating in 2008 and 2010 respectively. He obtained his PhD in Pharmaceutical Engineering from the same institution in 2015, with a dissertation on multivariate monitoring of aqueous film-coating processes. He joined the Department of Pharmaceutical Engineering as a Teaching Assistant in 2011 and was promoted to Assistant Professor in 2017. His group focuses on applying design of experiments, principal component analysis, and multivariate statistical process control to solid dosage manufacturing, particularly pan coating and fluidised-bed coating unit operations. He teaches courses in pharmaceutical process engineering and quality-by-design. The group regularly uses a Glatt GPCG-1 laboratory fluidised-bed coater, a Bohle pan coater, and near-infrared and Raman in-line probes available at the faculty pilot plant.
open_to: contract research on film-coating process development and optimisation
joint projects involving process analytical technology implementation
equipment access to laboratory pan coater and fluidised-bed coater with in-line spectroscopic probes
student internships for companies wishing to explore QbD approaches to coating
consulting on design of experiments for pharmaceutical process characterisation
industrial PhD co-supervision
researchers.industry_experience: Orlović completed a three-month placement at Farmavita d.o.o., a generic pharmaceutical manufacturer in Sarajevo, during his doctoral studies in 2013, where he assisted with process validation documentation for a pan-coated tablet line. He has since carried out two short consulting engagements for regional pharmaceutical companies on coating process troubleshooting, though neither resulted in a formal contract.
researchers.notes: Orlović is actively seeking an industry partner for a planned application to the Innovation Fund of Serbia's Collaborative Grant scheme; a company willing to co-define a coating process challenge would be well-positioned to develop this together. His pilot-plant booking schedule is typically heaviest in the autumn semester; summer months offer more flexibility for joint experimental campaigns.

researchers.name: Snežana Todorović
researchers.title: Assistant Professor
researchers.department: Department of Computing and Control Engineering
researchers.bio: Snežana Todorović received her B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Computer Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2009 and 2011 respectively, and her Ph.D. from the same institution in 2017, with a thesis on distributed inverted-index structures for heterogeneous document corpora. She held a postdoctoral position at the University of Ljubljana between 2018 and 2019 before returning to Novi Sad as an Assistant Professor. Her group focuses on scalable full-text retrieval, approximate nearest-neighbour (ANN) search over dense vector embeddings, and hybrid sparse–dense index architectures suited for multilingual and multi-modal document collections. She teaches courses on database systems and information retrieval. The group operates within the Laboratory for Intelligent Data Systems at FTN, where they maintain a small GPU cluster and access shared HPC resources through the PARADOX-IV system.
open_to: joint projects with companies building internal search or document management systems
contract research on index architecture, ANN search tuning, or hybrid retrieval pipelines
industrial PhD supervision for candidates working on search infrastructure problems
student internships for final-year or master's students
consulting on search system scalability and evaluation methodology
researchers.industry_experience: Between 2011 and 2013, Todorović worked part-time as a backend engineer at a Novi Sad software house building a document archiving platform, where she was responsible for search indexing components. She has since collaborated informally with two local companies on search performance evaluations.
researchers.notes: Todorović is comfortable with projects that require access to sensitive or non-public document collections under appropriate data-sharing agreements. She prefers collaborations where the research question is clearly defined before contracts are signed, and is cautious about engagements that would limit publication rights.

researchers.name: Nina Mamužić
researchers.title: Professor Emeritus
researchers.department: Department of Fruit Growing, Viticulture, Horticulture and Landscape Architecture
researchers.bio: Nina Mamužić received her BSc and MSc degrees from the Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad, and completed her PhD there in 1993 with a dissertation on flavonoid profiles in autochthonous berry crops of Vojvodina. She joined the Department of Fruit Growing, Viticulture, Horticulture and Landscape Architecture as an assistant professor in 1994 and was promoted to full professor in 2007, retiring in 2019 as Professor Emeritus. Her research group focused on secondary metabolite accumulation—particularly anthocyanins, rutin, and chlorogenic acid—in elderberry (Sambucus nigra) accessions collected across the Pannonian Plain, with a sustained interest in how seasonal drought modifies these pathways. Teaching responsibilities included courses in small fruit production and plant biochemistry. Laboratory work relied on HPLC-DAD, spectrophotometric DPPH assays, and controlled drought chambers at the faculty's pomology laboratory.
open_to: consulting
researchers.industry_experience: Between 2005 and 2014, Professor Mamužić provided informal technical advice to two small elderberry processing cooperatives in Srem on raw material sourcing and drying protocols, though these engagements were not formalised as contracts. She has no other recorded industry partnerships.
researchers.notes: Professor Mamužić is fully retired and is not available for project leadership, supervision of doctoral students, or laboratory work. She is willing to consult on elderberry phytochemistry, Pannonian accession selection, and irrigation-based polyphenol enhancement strategies for companies working with elderberry raw materials or extracts. Contact is best arranged through the department, as she checks email infrequently. She retains access to the faculty's archived chromatographic data from the 1995–2016 period, which could be of value to companies seeking historical baseline datasets for the region.

researchers.name: Jelena Marković
researchers.title: Full Professor
researchers.bio: Jelena Marković is a Full Professor at the University of Novi Sad's Faculty of Technology, Department of Food Preservation Engineering. Her research integrates food engineering, packaging science, and predictive microbiology to extend the shelf life of perishable horticultural products, with a particular focus on Serbian soft fruits. She has extensive experience developing modified atmosphere packaging systems and mathematical models for microbial growth kinetics in cold-chain logistics. Professor Marković has collaborated with multiple Serbian fruit exporters on industrial packaging trials and serves as an academic partner on the FRESHROUTE innovation project targeting cold-chain optimization for berry exports. She is actively open to industrial PhD supervision and joint research projects with industry.

researchers.name: Krisztina Kiss
researchers.title: Full Professor
researchers.department: Department of Computing and Control Engineering
researchers.bio: Krisztina Kiss received her Dipl.Ing. degree in computer engineering from the University of Novi Sad in 2001 and her PhD in electrical and computer engineering from the same institution in 2008, with a dissertation on statistical traffic profiling in industrial Ethernet networks. She joined the Department of Computing and Control Engineering as an assistant professor in 2009 and was promoted to full professor in 2020. Her research group focuses on unsupervised anomaly detection and one-class classification for industrial control system protocol traffic, using statistical baseline modelling, kernel methods, and lightweight online learning algorithms suited to constrained embedded environments. She teaches courses on network security, operating systems, and industrial communication protocols. The group operates a dedicated ICS testbed equipped with Siemens-compatible PLCs, Modbus/TCP and DNP3 traffic generators, and packet capture infrastructure for long-term dataset collection.
open_to: joint projects with companies deploying ICS monitoring solutions
contract research on protocol traffic analysis and anomaly detection deployment
industrial PhD supervision for candidates from companies in automation and critical infrastructure
student internships on ICS testbed experiments and dataset collection
consulting on detector calibration, evaluation methodology, and deployment architecture for industrial networks
access to ICS testbed and long-term traffic capture infrastructure for collaborative experiments
researchers.industry_experience: Kiss has collaborated with a regional energy distributor and a water utility as monitoring data partners on two funded projects, providing practical validation of research methods on operational infrastructure. She has carried out paid consulting for a mid-size automation integrator on specifying anomaly detection requirements for a SCADA upgrade project.
researchers.notes: Kiss prefers applied collaborations that result in deployment on real infrastructure rather than purely synthetic experiments. Her group's testbed capacity is available to industrial partners under a data-sharing agreement. She is particularly interested in partners dealing with proprietary or undocumented ICS protocols, which represent a gap in her current work.

researchers.name: Vuk Đukić
researchers.title: Associate Professor
researchers.department: Department of Computing and Control Engineering
researchers.bio: Vuk Đukić is an Associate Professor at the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, within the Department of Computing and Control Engineering. His research focuses on cybersecurity and network security, with particular emphasis on intrusion detection, anomaly detection in industrial control systems, IoT security, and threat modelling. He has led and contributed to multiple national and international research initiatives aimed at securing critical infrastructure and smart environments. Professor Đukić has published in reputable journals and conferences and is actively involved in interdisciplinary collaboration with industry. He is open to supervising industrial PhD students and engaging in joint research projects with technology companies seeking expertise in operational technology security and advanced threat analysis.
